title: LLM caching & KV-prefix cache — scratchpad / mini PRD
content:
Purpose / context:
Quick personal scratchpad to capture an idea for improving latency/cost for common LLM patterns by introducing a lightweight KV-prefix cache and more explicit topology-aware prefix routing.

Problem we see in prod:
- Many customers have a small set of repeated prompts/prefixes (instructions, system prompts, few-shot examples) that account for a disproportionate share of tokens on the first few positions.
- Current prefix/KV cache is generic but coarse-grained; misses opportunities for:
  * evicting less-important prefixes faster,
  * storing compressed/quantized KV slices for hot prefixes,
  * routing requests with hot prefixes to warm pools (reduce cold-start tokens).
- Result: increased p99 latency on tail of sessions, higher cost due to repeated decode of same KV for similar prompts.

Goal / success metrics (rough):
- Reduce per-request effective token cost for sessions with repeated prefixes by 20–40% (measured on sampled workloads).
- Reduce median & p95 decode latency for warm-prefix requests by ~15–30ms (platform SLO target dependent).
- Keep added memory overhead < 10% on average per serving instance.

Key idea: KV-prefix cache + prefix-aware routing
- Maintain a small, LRU/TTL-backed store of KV-cache fragments keyed by (model, model-version, prefix-hash, prefix-type).
- Provide API hints (from SDK or routing policy) marking a request as "prefix-hot" with a small affinity token so the router can select warm pools.
- Support two storage modes: in-memory hot KV (fast) and compressed cold store (lz4/quantized) to rehydrate into memory asynchronously.
- Eviction policy tuned for prefix hit-rate and token-cost-saved estimate (not just recency).

Assumptions and constraints:
- We can add small SDK/HTTP header (x-rw-prefix-hint) without breaking backwards compat.
- Routing layer can be augmented to consider an affinity header within current policy infra (policy engine + smart routing).
- Serving runtime exposes primitives to pre-populate KV cache for a session (existing code mostly supports this).
- Security: KV cache contains only non-sensitive de-duplicated activations; still need to confirm PII/tenant isolation with security.

User stories (rough):
- As an app developer, when I send a prompt with a known system instruction, the platform should serve it from a warm pool with pre-populated KV so my first tokens have lower latency and cost.
- As SRE, I want to see prefix hit-rate and cost-saved metrics per route so we can tune policies and billing.
- As product, I want an option to opt-in per-route or globally to avoid surprising changes for customers.

Design notes / components:
1) Prefix detection & hints:
   - SDK helper: Redwood SDK exposes markPrefix(prefixText) that returns prefix-hash; server adds header.
   - Heuristic detector at edge (optional) that extracts repeated prefix in request history.
2) KV-prefix cache store:
   - Key = model|ver|prefix-hash|tenant-scope, maintain metadata: hit_count, last_access, token_position_range, estimated_cpu_saved
   - Eviction: score = alpha*estimated_savings + beta*recency - gamma*memory_cost
3) Router integration:
   - If header present and matching warm-pool available, route to pool with preloaded KV and warm instance tag.
   - Fallback: normal routing w/ async rehydrate request to warm pool (background).
4) Serving runtime changes:
   - API to load KV fragment into instance memory for model variant.
   - Fast path check to use preloaded KV when session starts.
5) Observability & billing:
   - New metrics: prefix_hit, prefix_miss, bytes_rehydrated, cost_saved_tokens, warm_pool_affinity_rate
   - Dashboard per-route and exported to billing pipeline (optionally show cost-savings to customers).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Security: confirm no tenant cross-contamination; prefix fragments must be tenant-scoped and maybe encrypted in cold store. Action: ping Security (Mariana).
- SDK change scope: how intrusive is markPrefix and do we support auto-detection? (Ravi to prototype).
- Memory accounting: what's the realistic overhead for common models (Llama2-13B, Mistral, etc.)? Need bench data from serving-runtime team.
- Pricing model: do we charge for warm-prefix storage? might be part of dedicated features. Product decision.

Prototype plan (short, minimal):
- Week 0–1: small spike — simulate frequent prefixes using existing KV cache hooks, measure hit rates and potential savings on sampled logs (Ravi).
- Week 2: implement header + router affinity prototype (edge routing config, fallback path).
- Week 3: runtime primitive to preload small KV fragment (engineering spike, see PR #512 for reference).
- Week 4: internal dogfood on a few internal routes, collect metrics and iterate.

Notes to self / parking lot ideas:
- Could combine with model-variant quantized prefix store (store prefix KV in int8 for giant models).
- Consider user-visible API to pin a prefix TTL for a route (like reserved caching).
- Possible synergy with Redwood Optimize recommendations: detect high-benefit prefixes and suggest enabling feature.

Links / references:
- GH PR with KV prepopulate spike: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/512
- Related Confluence doc: CONFLUENCE-9876 (prefix-cache design notes, internal)
- Jira: JIRA-3245 (prefix-affinity routing epic)

Immediate next actions (this week):
- Share this scratchpad with Ravi + Mariana and schedule 30m sync (done?)
- Ravi: run sampling job on logs to surface top-200 prefixes by token-volume (assignee: Ravi)
- Me (Ava): draft short RFC if spike looks promising, include cost model and SLO impact.

Random half-baked thoughts:
- Could we use ephemeral GPU instance warmers that only hold KV (cheap memory-only pool)?
- Maybe prefix signatures should include normalization (strip timestamps, user ids) so hits generalize.

End of scratchpad. Will refine into more formal PRD if spikes show good ROI.
